network: fixture pages load from file:// URLs — no HTTP server and no IP networking are involved. Chromium's Fetch interception (offline/cdp-drive.mjs) refuses every non-file request (recorded per viewport as externalRequests, asserted zero), and the in-page bootstrap independently refuses requests: fetch is rejected, and XHR open() records the attempt while send() is refused in-page with the refusal labeled in the report's xhrRefused list — the native open/send are never invoked (ADOPT-B2-R1; proven by the control-xhr controlled page in controls). Zero attempts are asserted per case. (A loopback HTTP origin was tried first; Chrome 152's Local Network Access checks refuse even the navigation to it in this environment, net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_LOCAL_NETWORK_ACCESS_CHECKS, so the evidence uses file://.)
clock: each page freezes Date at the case's independent receipt instant (see responses/*.json: frozenClock + clockSource from the handler run). The checker's settle budget is measured on performance.now (monotonic elapsed time), so the wait expires and emits its report even though Date is frozen (ADOPT-B2-R1); each report records settle.budgetMs / settle.elapsedMs / settle.outcome. Chart validation is series-bound (ADOPT-B2-R2): shapes under defs/axis/grid/legend/tooltip/reference ancestors are decorations, a valid series mark needs finite geometry with positive extent on both axes, and the valid count is bound to the fixture's nonzero net-GEX rows (packet expect.minSeriesMarks) — zero rows may render collapsed and are never required to have pixels. Controls are judged by the intended-negative gate in offline/browser-controls.mjs (classifyControlReport): an expected-negative MATCH requires exactly the chart assertion to fail, all unrelated assertions to pass, a consistent summary, the matching case, and the declared settle outcome; malformed/missing reports are BLOCKED and fail the run; aggregationProof records the synthetic counterexamples the gate was proven against.
